title: The Azure DLP integration through Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding: separate versus shared credentials, templates, roles and the automatically created integration

prose.text: The shared integration object is in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration]]; the Azure resources common to this path and the Zscaler Incident Receiver path (Event Grid, data-container read, manual storage networking, Front Door) are in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration.resources]], and the ZIA-side onboarding in [[zia.dlp.cloud-to-cloud-forwarding]].

checks.do: Whether the deployment uses separate service principals or shared credentials, which decides the template, the role JSON and whether an integration already exists.
Whether the storage account name contains dots.

overview-no-appliances.statement: Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding sends DLP incident metadata and evidence files to the organization's Azure storage containers without deploying appliances.

quotes: Workflow Automation DLP application integration with an Azure instance using Zscaler Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding enables your organization to send Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incident metadata and evidence files to your organization's Azure storage containers in your Azure account without deploying appliances.

auth-modes.statement: The integration can use separate service principals for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Workflow Automation, or shared credentials between them (certificate-based authentication).

quotes: You can configure the Workflow Automation DLP application integration to use separate service principals for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Workflow Automation, or to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation (i.e., certificate-based authentication).

client-certificate-optional.statement: The Azure client certificate is generated with the aes_certificate.sh shell script when shared credentials are wanted, by creating a private key and self-signed certificate in Azure; otherwise the step is not required.

quotes: 1. (Optional) Generate the Azure client certificate using the aes_certificate.sh shell script in Azure.

If you want to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation (i.e., certificate-based authentication), you must generate a private key and self-signed certificate in Azure. Otherwise, this step is not required.

script-and-templates.statement: The Cloud-to-Cloud path uses the create-app-registration-c2c.sh script, with the ZscalerAzureIntegrationRM_C2C.json template for separate service principals and ZscalerAzureIntegrationRM_C2C_shared.json for shared credentials.

quotes: Click the create-app-registration-c2c.sh link to download the Zscaler Bash script.

If you want to use separate service principals for Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation, click the ZscalerAzureIntegrationRM_C2C.json link to download the Azure DLP Integration resource manager template.
if you want to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation (i.e., certificate-based authentication), click the ZscalerAzureIntegrationRM_C2C_shared.json link.

storage-account-name-no-dots.statement: The storage account name for the Cloud-to-Cloud template deployment and for the manual storage account creation must not contain dots (.).

quotes: Storage Account Name: Enter the name of the storage account. Ensure that you do not use dots (.) in the storage account name.
Storage account name: Enter a name for your storage account. Ensure that you do not use dots (.) in the storage account name.

owner-permission.statement: On the Cloud-to-Cloud page the deploying user needs Owner permission in Azure, because role definitions and assignments are added during the procedure.

quotes: Log in to the Azure portal as a user with Owner permission in Azure. Owner permission is required because you add role definitions and assignments during this procedure.

resource-group-vm-reference.statement: The Cloud-to-Cloud page's manual resource-group step says the resource group must be the same one used for creating the VM, although the page says it works without deploying appliances.
resource-group-vm-reference.conditions: A vendor documentation defect, not a tool behavior; not filed. No quote states that the page creates no VM; that rests on a case-insensitive search of this capture for 'the VM', which returns only this line.

quotes: Resource group: From the drop-down menu, select an existing resource group. The resource group must be the same one you used for creating the VM.
without deploying appliances

upstream.note: help.zscaler.com Configuring the Azure DLP Application Integration Using Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding: the manual resource-group step refers to 'the VM' on a path with no VM.

containers.statement: On the Cloud-to-Cloud path the data and metadata containers are named <storageAccountNamePrefix>-data and <storageAccountNamePrefix>-metadata, and the Zscaler DLP Incident Management service reads and stores the incident metadata file (with trigger data stripped) but never reads or stores the incident data files; the manual procedure says two containers must be created for the storage account.

quotes: After the storage account successfully deploys, you must create two containers for the storage account.

The names of the data and metadata containers are set to <storageAccountNamePrefix>-data and <storageAccountNamePrefix>-metadata, respectively. The Zscaler DLP Incident Management service reads and stores the incident metadata file (with trigger data stripped), but it never reads or stores the incident data files.

role-by-mode.statement: The custom role JSON depends on the mode: for separate service principals it lists container read, generateUserDelegationKey and Event Grid eventSubscriptions write/read/delete actions with the blobs read data action; for shared credentials the JSON lists containers write among its actions and blobs read and blobs write among its dataActions.

quotes: If you are using separate service principals for Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation, click Edit and replace the action parameters that appear by default with the following JSON.

"actions": [ "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read", "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/generateUserDelegationKey/action", "Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics/eventSubscriptions/write",

"Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics/eventSubscriptions/read", "Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics/eventSubscriptions/delete" ], "dataActions": [ "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/read" ]
If you are using shared credentials between Internet & SaaS andWorkflow Automation, click Edit and replace the action parameters that appear by default with the following JSON.

"Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read", "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/write", "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/generateUserDelegationKey/action",
"dataActions": [ "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/read", "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/write" ]

shared-credentials-auto-integration.statement: With shared credentials, onboarding an Azure tenant in Internet & SaaS automatically adds a DLP Azure integration in disabled state, which is edited instead of adding a new one; with separate service principals a new integration is added. The ZIA-side page adds the condition that the Azure application tenant was onboarded for Workflow Automation (the optional Workflow Automation checkbox) and that a private key was used.
shared-credentials-auto-integration.conditions: Automatic creation needs the tenant to be onboarded for Workflow Automation and a private key to be used, per the ZIA-side Azure page (zia.dlp.cloud-to-cloud-forwarding:azure-zwa).

quotes: If you are using separate service principals for Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation, you need to add a new DLP Azure integration.

If you are using shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation, after you onboard an Azure tenant in Internet & SaaS, a new DLP Azure integration in disabled state is automatically added for you.
In this case, edit that DLP Azure integration instead of adding a new integration.
(Optional) To onboard with Workflow Automation, select the Workflow Automation checkbox.

If you have onboarded the Azure application tenant for Workflow Automation, and used a private key, a new DLP Azure integration in disabled state is automatically added for you in Workflow Automation.

synced-fields.statement: For the integration that Internet & SaaS creates automatically, the integration name is the tenant name (editable), and the Enterprise Tenant ID and Tenant Name in the ZIA Tenant Information section are synced from Internet & SaaS; Enable Integration changes the status to Enabled.

quotes: The integrations that Internet & SaaS automatically creates use the tenant name as the DLP application integration name.
the Integration Name that appears is synced from Internet & SaaS. You can edit the name.
Enterprise Tenant ID: The tenant ID that is created when configuring DLP cloud-to-cloud incident forwarding in Internet & SaaS appears. This value is synced from Internet & SaaS.
Tenant Name: The tenant name that was used when configuring DLP cloud-to-cloud incident forwarding in Internet & SaaS appears. This value that appears is synced from Internet & SaaS.
Click Enable Integration. The status of the integration changes to Enabled.

shared-no-client-secret.statement: When using shared credentials, the manual app registration does not need the client secret steps after the registration details are saved.

quotes: If you want to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation (i.e., certificate-based authentication), then the remaining steps are not required.
Next to the Client credentials, click Add a certificate or secret.
On the Certificates & secrets page, click New client secret.
